name: Golden Smog
label: Twin/Tone
lede: A Flintstones nickname, five covers, a fake name for everyone, and an Uncle Tupelo refugee in Dan Murphy's basement: Minneapolis's side-project band that outlasted most of the main ones.

eras.title: Ponchos, driftwood lamps, and a bar-band joke
eras.text: Minneapolis in the hardcore years, and a few future Soul Asylum and Jayhawks players decide the most annoying thing they can do is play the Eagles straight. The joke grows a name and a lineup.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: [[Dan Murphy|06806bee-5233-4c4e-b644-2243620278db]] and [[Dave Pirner|8849e71c-181b-444b-8cfb-09445e6231d4]] play the Eagles at the Uptown Bar
years.p: The band is called Take It to the Limit, and the point is to annoy a room full of hardcore fans.
years.xp:
Murphy, Pirner, Martin Zellar and Jim Boquist played the Uptown Bar in January 1987 as an Eagles tribute. Murphy remembers the costume: "We wore ponchos and had driftwood lamps [onstage] -- just to kind of piss everybody off."

Around 1989 the same crowd did two Rolling Stones tribute nights, "Exile On Lake Street" at the Uptown and "His Satanic Majesties Paycheck" at the Cabooze.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Three guitarists, one acoustic set, the name on the marquee at the 400 Bar
years.p: Kraig Johnson, Murphy and [[Gary Louris|dd3e4c5c-b2fa-4614-9351-28362e31d015]] play covers of Jim Croce, the Monkees and Neil Diamond: the first show billed as Golden Smog.
years.xp: The name comes from a Flintstones episode in which Fred Flintstone gets a nickname that parodies Mel Torme's "Velvet Fog." Louris credits Murphy with picking it; Murphy says a girl he knew told him she'd use it if she ever had a band.

q: None of us were that famous to begin with.
years.src: Daily Vault: Marc Perlman interview · No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: [[Marc Perlman|f0e45a77-5231-4cc6-8131-27b44ff3169b]] and [[Chris Mars|b0fefe3c-b393-4498-9b33-255b02d75716]] plug in for the Cabooze shows
years.p: Perlman takes bass; Mars, just out of the Replacements, takes drums.
years.xp: Perlman's version: Pirner was supposed to drum but backed out the day of the first practice, then a miscommunication had him call Mars instead. On the supergroup label, Perlman says: "None of us were that famous to begin with."

eras.title: Five covers and a fake name each
eras.text: A small label offers to press the bar-band act, and the members hide behind pseudonyms. The record is a covers EP cut at Pachyderm, the studio in Cannon Falls.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · Twin/Tone Records: Golden Smog · Discogs: On Golden Smog (2022 reissue)
years.h: On Golden Smog EP: five covers, Bad Company to Thin Lizzy
years.p: Pirner sings Bad Company's "Shooting Star"; Louris takes the song from the musical Hair.
years.xp:
The five tracks are Bad Company, the Rolling Stones, Thin Lizzy, Hair and Michaelangelo covers, cut at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota. Crackpot Records issued it; Rykodisc reissued it in 1996, and a 5,500-copy Record Store Day vinyl followed on April 23, 2022.

Wikipedia dates the release to December 11, 1992; Twin/Tone's catalog page carries the EP too.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Country Standard Time: This Smog is Golden
years.h: Pirner is Anthony James; Louris is Michael Macklyn
years.p: Everyone is credited with a middle name plus the street they grew up on.
years.xp:
The EP credits Pirner as Anthony James, Murphy as David Spear-Way, Johnson as Jarret Decatur-Laine, Perlman as Raymond Virginia-Circle, Mars (who drew the cover) as Eddie Garfield-Avenue, and Louris as Michael Macklyn-Drive. Murphy says the system came from how Bon Jovi checked into hotels.

A 1998 Country Standard Time piece said the pseudonyms on the 1996 album were for legal reasons. Johnson's take on dropping them for Weird Tales: "we could record under our real names, and people still wouldn't know who we are."

eras.title: Tweedy walks into the basement
eras.text: Uncle Tupelo splits, Jeff Tweedy needs somewhere to be, and Murphy has a studio in his basement. The first real Golden Smog album gets made in five days and sits on a shelf for over a year.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: Murphy calls [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]]: come write in my basement
years.p: Uncle Tupelo broke up on May 1, 1994. Murphy's offer arrived two months later.
years.xp:
Murphy: "I've got a studio in my basement, if you want to come over and do some writing... You could stay at the house." Tweedy recalls being "really happy and kind of shocked that they asked me to do it." Louris recalls: "Jeff was really blown away by the respect and the support he got from us at a time when he was in a little bit of a fragile state."

Murphy also booked the 400 Club on July 25, 1994, billed as Circle the Drain, to try out new songs. The link ran both ways: Louris played on three tracks of Uncle Tupelo's Still Feel Gone in 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia: On Golden Smog · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.p: Pirner's vocal on the 1992 EP cover of Bad Company's "Shooting Star" ends up in Kevin Smith's 1994 film.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Down by the Old Mainstream
years.h: Down by the Old Mainstream: recorded in five days, held for a year
years.p: Tweedy contributes "Pecan Pie" and, billed as Scot Summit, plays bass and guitar; Rykodisc releases it.
years.xp: The band cut it at Pachyderm in October 1994 with no rehearsals: "We'd just sit together and jam for a while and then say, 'Let's roll tape,'" Murphy says. Tweedy wrote "Pecan Pie" and "Walk Where He Walked" and co-wrote "Radio King" with Louris; Murphy brought "Ill Fated." No Depression puts the release at January 1996, after more than a year on the shelf.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm
years.h: Lounge Ax to LoDo: a six-month tour for a side project
years.p: It starts at Chicago's Lounge Ax and ends at Denver's LoDo Festival on August 2, 1996.
years.xp: Murphy, on why the band existed: "It's a chance to be foolish again; to go out and have frivolous fun, to tour and not have any responsibility." He also called himself an "emotional basket case" going in and said the tour was "really pure."

years.src: Country Standard Time: This Smog is Golden · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: [[Jody Stephens|0acfc6ca-d0b4-4f9e-a1a1-31c5fb2556bc]] of Big Star sits in on New Year's Eve in Chicago
years.p: He'd soon be the band's drummer.

eras.title: Bummed-out guys in Memphis
eras.text: The follow-up gets made at Ardent in Memphis, and it is darker than anyone planned. Real names replace the pseudonyms.

years.src: No Depression: Golden Smog, Shelter From The Storm · Wikipedia: Weird Tales (album)
years.h: Weird Tales: Ardent Studios, Stephens on drums, real names on the sleeve
years.p: It carries a 1933 pulp-magazine cover by Margaret Brundage and Brian Paulson's production.
years.xp:
Two Memphis sessions, January 1997 (under two weeks) and February 1998, plus time at Murphy's Terrarium in Minneapolis. Johnson: "After we did the first session, I went home and I listened to it and I thought, 'These are some bummed-out guys.'" Murphy: "It's darker, definitely."

Stephens joined as his father was ill with lung cancer; he says the support from the band was "pretty remarkable." Louris and Tweedy shared a room in Memphis and spent the first night wondering what they were doing there, then stayed up talking after the first studio day.

eras.title: Spain, a Kinks cover, and no Tweedy
eras.text: After eight quiet years the band reconvenes in southern Spain, then makes a record without Tweedy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Another Fine Day · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Another Fine Day: recorded in Spain with producer Paco Loco
years.p: Lost Highway releases it eight years after Weird Tales, with a cover of the Kinks' "Strangers."
years.xp: Recorded at Paco Loco's studio in El Puerto de Santa Maria. Tweedy and Jody Stephens appear alongside Ed Ackerson, drummer Linda Pitmon and a local brass section. Pitchfork gave it 6.4.

years.h: Blood on the Slacks: the first Smog record without Tweedy
years.p: Louris, Murphy, Johnson and Perlman add guests [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] and Pirner; the title nods at Dylan's Blood on the Tracks.

years.src: Owl and Bear: Dan Murphy interview · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Murphy explains why they never play: five managers, five cities
years.p: Stay Golden, Smog, a Rykodisc best-of with unreleased tracks, is out the same year.
years.xp: Murphy said the band rarely toured because of "five different management companies involved and five different cities that people live in." The compilation includes a Brian Wilson cover.

eras.title: Back at First Avenue
eras.text: A birthday party turns into a real reunion. Tweedy returns and Steve Gorman takes the drum stool.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golden Smog · Star Tribune: Golden Smog reunion
years.h: Murphy's 57th birthday party is his first gig since Soul Asylum
years.p: Golden Smog reunites privately; he left Soul Asylum in 2012.

years.src: Star Tribune: Golden Smog reunion · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: First Avenue, two nights, Tweedy back for the first time since 2011
years.p: The shows celebrate the club's 52nd anniversary and had been postponed since April 2020.
years.xp: Louris, Perlman, Murphy, Johnson and Stephens are all there. Murphy on the delay: "A little more time to try to get our [stuff] together again."

years.src: BrooklynVegan: Golden Smog NYC-area shows · Wikipedia: Golden Smog
years.h: Jersey City, the Bowery, then Chicago: first shows outside Minnesota in about twenty years
years.p: Steve Gorman of the Black Crowes drums; Tweedy plays as a sixth member.
years.xp: White Eagle Hall in Jersey City on December 5, Bowery Ballroom on December 6, the Vic in Chicago on December 9. The sets leaned on the first two albums and included covers of Brian Wilson, David Bowie, Neil Young, Eddie and the Hot Rods and the Kinks. Gorman had sat in during a 2023 holiday show and became a member in 2024.
